air_quality: Annual mean PM2.5 (2025) at the nearest EPA AQS regulatory monitor in Utah (23 monitors; straight-line distance, mean across monitors' POCs). Towns have no monitor of their own, so distance to assigned monitor in km: salt-lake-city:3km, west-valley-city:2km, west-jordan:4km, provo:11km, orem:5km, sandy:6km, st-george:25km, ogden:9km, layton:19km, south-jordan:5km, lehi:13km, millcreek:5km, taylorsville:3km, herriman:2km, logan:12km, murray:1km, draper:9km, bountiful:2km, riverton:9km, spanish-fork:2km, roy:16km, pleasant-grove:3km, cedar-city:8km, kaysville:15km, cottonwood-heights:8km, holladay:6km, eagle-mountain:20km, saratoga-springs:17km, american-fork:8km, park-city:19km, heber-city:2km, midway:7km, moab:1km, vernal:3km, price:4km, tooele:9km, brigham-city:3km, richfield:142km, kanab:71km, hurricane:1km, washington:19km, ephraim:74km.
commute_minutes: 2020–2024 ACS mean one-way travel time to work for workers age 16+ who do not work at home. Calculated from aggregate travel minutes (B08013) divided by commuting workers (B08303), rounded to one decimal. Place-level estimates; no county substitutions.
crime_rate: Reported NIBRS offenses against persons and against property (excludes crimes against society, e.g. drug offenses) divided by the reporting agency's stable resident population, x1000, from the Utah BCI Crime in Utah 2024 report. 'Persons' includes simple assault, so this is broader than UCR violent+index property. Notes: millcreek uses Unified Police Dept. of Greater Salt Lake (shared/county jurisdiction rate); bountiful uses 2023 report (no 2024 data submitted); holladay uses Unified Police Dept. of Greater Salt Lake (shared/county jurisdiction rate); eagle-mountain uses Utah County Sheriff (shared/county jurisdiction rate); midway uses Wasatch County Sheriff (shared/county jurisdiction rate).
flood_risk: FEMA National Risk Index inland-flooding Risk Index score (expected annual loss scaled by social vulnerability and community resilience, national percentile 0-100), averaged over the census tracts inside the town weighted by population. Tracts are assigned to a town when the tract centroid is inside the UGRC municipal outline; moab, richfield, kanab, ephraim had no tract centroid inside and take the tract containing the town center. Measured, not estimated, for all 42 towns.
home_value: Median value of owner-occupied housing units (U.S. Census Bureau American Community Survey 5-year estimates, table DP04), as reported per place; every one of the 42 towns has a place-level ACS estimate, so no county-level proxy was needed.
job_growth: Change in annual-average employment (all industries, all ownerships) in the town's county from 2021 to 2024, from the BLS Quarterly Census of Employment and Wages. QCEW does not publish these towns separately, so every town takes its county's value.
median_income: Median household income (U.S. Census Bureau American Community Survey 5-year estimates, table S1901), as reported per place; every one of the 42 towns has a place-level ACS estimate, so no county-level proxy was needed.
median_rent: Median gross rent (U.S. Census Bureau American Community Survey 5-year estimates, table DP04), as reported per place; every one of the 42 towns has a place-level ACS estimate, so no county-level proxy was needed. Small towns' estimates carry wider margins of error given smaller renter-occupied samples.
national_parks: Modeled driving distance in miles to the nearest Utah National Park (Mighty 5) or premier State Park based on road detour factors.
net_migration: Domestic plus international net migration into the town's county over the four years July 2020 to July 2024, per 1,000 residents at July 2020. The Census Bureau publishes migration components for counties only, so every town takes its county's value (13 Salt Lake County towns share one value, and so on).
noise: PROXY, not measured noise: straight-line distance from the town center point to the nearest interstate highway (OSM highway=motorway with ref 'I-') or airport with an IATA code (OSM aeroway=aerodrome), whichever is closer. Larger = farther from major transport noise sources. Measured at a single city-center point, so large towns that span highways are understated. Components (km, interstate/airport): salt-lake-city:I=1.8,A=5.4 west-valley-city:I=3.4,A=8.5 west-jordan:I=2.8,A=17.4 provo:I=1.8,A=4.6 orem:I=2.6,A=7.6 sandy:I=5.0,A=24.6 st-george:I=0.2,A=7.2 ogden:I=2.4,A=2.8 layton:I=0.5,A=4.8 south-jordan:I=2.6,A=22.7 lehi:I=0.9,A=20.1 millcreek:I=3.6,A=12.9 taylorsville:I=1.2,A=11.1 herriman:I=11.6,A=28.5 logan:I=24.8,A=6.5 murray:I=1.1,A=12.7 draper:I=2.3,A=28.0 bountiful:I=1.3,A=4.2 riverton:I=4.0,A=27.1 spanish-fork:I=0.8,A=11.3 roy:I=0.3,A=2.4 pleasant-grove:I=2.8,A=14.4 cedar-city:I=1.6,A=3.2 kaysville:I=0.7,A=7.8 cottonwood-heights:I=1.9,A=21.2 holladay:I=1.6,A=15.9 eagle-mountain:I=16.3,A=25.2 saratoga-springs:I=7.9,A=19.3 american-fork:I=0.8,A=16.7 park-city:I=8.6,A=40.9 heber-city:I=25.4,A=40.1 midway:I=23.3,A=37.5 moab:I=40.6,A=25.6 vernal:I=144.4,A=1.4 price:I=78.3,A=4.6 tooele:I=14.8,A=36.9 brigham-city:I=3.6,A=5.0 richfield:I=1.0,A=2.8 kanab:I=73.9,A=3.1 hurricane:I=9.4,A=22.5 washington:I=0.8,A=8.2 ephraim:I=36.2,A=42.2.
owner_occupancy: Owner-occupied housing units divided by all occupied housing units (ACS table B25003, place level, all 42 towns measured directly). A higher share means more long-term residents with a stake in the neighborhood.
population_growth: Percent change in the town's resident population from the April 2020 estimates base to the July 2024 estimate. Place-level for all 42 towns, no county proxy. Shows how fast a town is attracting residents.
price_to_income: Median home value divided by median household income: roughly how many years of the typical household's income it takes to buy the typical home here. Derived entirely from this repo's existing home_value.json and median_income.json (both 2023 Census ACS 5-year estimates), no new data retrieved. Lower is more affordable.
rent_burden: Median gross rent annualized (×12) divided by median household income: the share of the typical household's income the typical rent here would consume. Derived entirely from this repo's existing median_rent.json and median_income.json (both 2023 Census ACS 5-year estimates), no new data retrieved. Lower is more affordable. A common affordability guideline is that paying more than 0.30 (30%) of income on rent is considered cost-burdened.
restaurants_per_1k: OSM restaurant/cafe features within a 5 km straight-line radius of the town center, divided by the full town population from data/cities.json. This is nearby access per resident, not an administrative-boundary business density. Neighboring towns can share venues. Mapping completeness varies; ways/relations use bounding-box centers. OSM snapshot 2026-11-07T01:08:28Z.
schools: Four-year cohort graduation rate from the Utah State Board of Education (USBE) 2025 Graduation Rates Report, mapped to each town's public school district.
ski_access: Modeled driving time in minutes to the nearest Utah ski resort based on straight-line distances with mountain road routing and speed factors to resort coordinates.
sports: Straight-line km from town center to the nearest pro or NCAA Division I venue: Delta Center; America First Field; Rice-Eccles Stadium; LaVell Edwards Stadium; Maverik Center; Jon M. Huntsman Center; Dee Events Center; Stewart Stadium; Romney Stadium; Greater Zion Stadium; Cedar City: Eccles Coliseum; Utah Valley: UCCU Center; Smith Spectrum; Marriott Center.
tech_employers: Estimated count of tech establishments located within a straight-line 25 km radius of the town centroid, based on U.S. Census Bureau 2023 ZIP Code Business Patterns (ZBP) for NAICS 51 (Information sector proxy, including software publishers) and NAICS 5415 (Computer Systems Design and Related Services). Mapped strictly using official 2023 Census ZCTA Gazetteer centroid coordinates (unmatched PO-box ZIPs omitted as coverage gaps).
trails: Count of OpenStreetMap ways tagged with sac_scale (the hiking-difficulty tag applied to real trails, not urban sidewalks) whose highway type is path/footway/track/cycleway/bridleway, plus hiking/mountain-biking route relations, within 20km of the town center. Queried live from the Overpass API (Overpass QL: [out:json][timeout:50];(way["highway"~"^(path|footway|track|cycleway|bridleway)$"]["sac_scale"](around:20000,lat,lng);relation["route"~"^(hiking|mtb)$"](around:20000,lat,lng););out count;) on 2026-11-07, via https://maps.mail.ru/osm/tools/overpass/api/interpreter (raw per-town responses cached under data/raw/trails/<town-id>.json). draper re-queried separately on 2026-11-07, via https://maps.mail.ru/osm/tools/overpass/api/interpreter (raw per-town responses cached under data/raw/trails/<town-id>.json).
transit: UTA coverage only, not total public transit: Heber City has High Valley Transit route 106 (https://www.hvtutah.gov/bus-106-wasatch-back-connect-to-heber-valley), which is excluded from this UTA feed. A zero here does not mean no public transportation. Scheduled weekly (Mon-Sun) UTA transit departures per 1,000 residents, computed from UTA's real published GTFS feed (https://gtfsfeed.rideuta.com/GTFS.zip, feed_version 2026 AUG_20261008) by counting stop_times rows at every GTFS stop within 3km of the town centroid, for the representative week of 20260914-20260920, divided by town population and multiplied by 1000. Towns with 0 have no UTA stops within range, i.e. outside UTA's GTFS-covered service area: cedar-city, eagle-mountain, ephraim, heber-city, hurricane, kanab, logan, midway, moab, park-city, price, richfield, saratoga-springs, st-george, vernal, washington. That includes rural southern/eastern Utah towns UTA does not serve at all (moab, vernal, price, richfield, kanab, cedar-city, st-george, hurricane, washington, ephraim), some of which have separate regional systems (e.g. SunTran in St. George) not covered by this feed, plus a few towns just outside UTA's practical reach (park-city, heber-city, midway, logan, eagle-mountain, saratoga-springs) where the nearest GTFS stop is well beyond this radius.
unemployment_rate: Annual average unemployment rate for the town's county in 2024 (BLS Local Area Unemployment Statistics, not seasonally adjusted). BLS does not publish a series for most of these towns, so every town takes its county's rate.
university_access: Straight-line km from town center to the nearest of 10 Utah public/private universities and colleges: University of Utah; Utah State University; Brigham Young University; Weber State University; Southern Utah University; Utah Valley University; Utah Tech University; Westminster University; Snow College; Utah State University Eastern (Price). Coordinates from Wikipedia.
venues: OSM theatres, music venues, arts centres, galleries and museums within a 15 km straight-line radius of the canonical town center. Neighboring towns can share venues. Mapping completeness varies; ways/relations use bounding-box centers. OSM snapshot 2026-11-07T01:08:28Z.
water_quality: Count of EPA SDWIS health-based violations (MCL, treatment technique, etc.; is_health_based_ind=Y) whose compliance period began on/after 2021-11-06 for the town's primary community water system. Counts are per system, not normalised by size.
water_usage: System-level residential potable gallons per capita per day (GPCD) for the town's retail culinary water system, 2022 data. Potable only: towns with separate pressurized-irrigation (secondary) water (e.g. Lehi, Saratoga Springs) look low. Approximate system matches where the town has no own system: west-valley-city->Granger-Hunter Improvement District; millcreek->Salt Lake City Water System; cottonwood-heights->Jordan Valley Water Conservancy District (Retail); holladay->Holliday Water Co..
wildfire_risk: FEMA National Risk Index wildfire Risk Index score (expected annual loss scaled by social vulnerability and community resilience, national percentile 0-100), averaged over the census tracts inside the town weighted by population. Tracts are assigned to a town when the tract centroid is inside the UGRC municipal outline; moab, richfield, kanab, ephraim had no tract centroid inside and take the tract containing the town center. Measured, not estimated, for all 42 towns.
